summary: Repaired the cancelled revision 1 partial implementation so caught pre-promotion and post-promotion failures clean only invocation-owned artifacts and allow same-ID retry while preserving the v0.2 public materializer interface.

claims.claim: Current and immutable revision 2 contracts are byte-identical.
Caught Git failure before promotion removes the exact owned staging directory and lock and permits same-ID retry.
evidence: Failure-injection test observes an empty runs directory before a successful retry.

claims.claim: Caught receipt publication failure after promotion rolls back the invocation-owned final run, receipt, staging path, and lock and permits same-ID retry.
evidence: Revision 2 RED proved the cancelled partial implementation stranded the promoted run; final test confirms promotion occurred at injection and then observes an empty runs directory before retry.

claims.claim: Pre-existing final runs and receipts are never deleted or overwritten.
evidence: Checks run before and under the exclusive lock, receipt creation uses x mode, and rollback flags are set only after this invocation's successful creation/promotion.

claims.claim: The v0.2 function signature, receipt fields, exact dirty marker, Git status, and SHA-256 behavior are preserved.
evidence: All seven targeted materializer tests pass under root repetition.

uncertainty: Process termination or machine crash can still strand a lock, staging directory, or promoted run; safe stale-lock/crash recovery remains deferred.
external_calls: Local Git and Python subprocesses inside automatically cleaned temporary fixture runs.
